answer.evidence: This is a full 16x16 terrain tile: a 2-row light green grass band (rows 0-1) over a dark teal water fill (rows 2-15). It is a flat ground/water autotile with no standing volume, no front-edge line or eave shadow, and no vertical front face. The only features are the grass-to-water transition at rows 1-2 and a single light pixel at about row 12. It reads as a flat top-down tile, which is normal for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small dark teal block with only a few lighter specks, and the rest is large flat dark fill. The facts back this up: 38% near-flat coverage against 0% for both references, and only 8 distinct colours in total against 80 for the grass reference. The 8 visible tones per tile are not a real advantage, because they come from a handful of sparse dots on a flat base rather than from grass tufts, clumps or soil grain. The grass reference has varied tufts and several greens in every tile, and the paving reference has shaded stones with mortar lines. The candidate has no tufts, no grain and no per-area variation. Its edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is not near-black, but there is no real outline structure either. Overall it reads as a flat sticker-like fill, clearly shallower than the references.
